answer: One anti-Sybil mechanism is a bonded identity with slashing: each agent locks real collateral to earn a single vote, and detected fraud forfeits that bond. An attacker who tries to wander among thousands of fake accounts must fund every one, so the cost scales linearly with the number of identities. Even a gale of new registrations will not crack the ledge of honest consensus, because weight comes from locked capital, not from how many names appear.
